Internals

The code-level companion to the architecture overview: how bytes on disk become a ranked search hit in the browser, function by function.

Each section below owns one file. Read them in order and you have traced every line of the runtime.

Boot: dispatch and wiring

run() handles subcommands (help, version, style, rules, template, upgrade) and returns; anything else falls through to serve(), which wires the runtime in a fixed order — each step only depends on the ones before it.

The data model and the scan

Three structs, all JSON-shaped for the wire:

  • Page — path (slash-relative), project (first path segment, "" for root files), title, headings, text (visible text capped at 2,000 chars), modTime.
  • Project — name, sorted pages, and updatedAt = the newest page's mtime.
  • Snapshot — root, alphabetically sorted projects (root pages first), pageCount, generatedAt.

Rebuild() is one filepath.WalkDir: it skips dot-directories and node_modules, keeps only .html/.htm files, and tolerates everything — unreadable entries are skipped, malformed HTML still parses (x/net/html accepts anything), and a missing <title> falls back to the filename. extract() walks the parsed DOM once, collecting the title, every heading, and visible text until the cap.

Concurrency contract

The snapshot is immutable. Rebuild builds a complete new one and swaps the pointer under a write lock; Current() takes a read lock only long enough to copy the pointer. Readers never wait on a scan, and a scan never waits on readers.

Serving: injection and SSE fan-out

Four Go 1.22 method-pattern routes: /api/index.json encodes the current snapshot; /__byakugan/* serves the embedded UI; /events is the SSE stream; / resolves pages. HTML responses pass through injectHTML, which finds the last </body> case-insensitively and inserts one deferred script tag — appending when no closing tag exists, so even sloppy documents get the overlay.

Live reload is a tiny fan-out: each connected browser gets a goroutine holding a buffered channel (capacity 4) registered in a map[chan string]struct{}. Broadcast does a non-blocking send to every channel — a slow or stuck subscriber is dropped rather than allowed to block the watcher callback. Disconnects clean up via request.Context().Done().

The watch loop

One fsnotify watcher covers the whole tree: addTree walks and registers every directory (skipping hidden ones and node_modules), and a Create event for a new directory re-runs addTree on it so future writes are seen. Debouncing is a single time.AfterFunc timer: every event resets it, and only 300 ms of silence lets it fire — an agent regenerating fifty files produces exactly one rebuild and one reload.

Search scoring, client-side

The query is split into tokens; a page matches only if every token appears somewhere. Weights are additive per token:

Match locationWeight
title, from the first character8
title, anywhere5
path3
any heading3
body text1

Hits sort by score, top 20 ship. The same score() ranks the landing search and the overlay drawer's filter, so both surfaces agree on what matters. Snippets center the first match; highlighting escapes both the HTML and the regex before wrapping matches in <mark>.

Self-update

Two verbs share one GitHub client: Check compares the running version against releases/latest and reports a newer tag; Upgrade downloads the artifact for the current OS/arch and replaces the executable in place. The startup path only ever calls Check, on a background goroutine, printing a single log line when an update exists — upgrading is always an explicit human action.
